limits: Native machine states and hatches are staged, not physically assembled multiblocks.
Heat-exchanger fixtures supply distilled water and collect steam through test doubles; native recipe selection, hot-fluid drain, cold-fluid hatch fill and onRunningTick remain real.
IC2 furnace has real input/power checks; EnderIO uses a task double to measure credited work and real RF withdrawal.
Forestry/Railcraft/Thaumcraft/induction adapter checks exercise transformed handler methods; they are not complete recipe throughput or GUI tests.
Native 5/16-tick polling and whole-batch boundaries can limit effective speed for short Forestry/Railcraft jobs.
UV countdown and plasma thermal cycles are probed; the remaining purification phases are wrapped through their native method bodies but not fully assembled or supply-timing tested.
IC2 lathe is player-driven with no recipe timer; Beam Crafter progress represents supplied particles. Both are intentionally unchanged.
When migrating an in-flight old purification cycle, completion fraction and existing phase state are retained; missed historical phase work is not fabricated.
